chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Tatum's reluctance to see Collins leave for Nat Cole
summary: Tatum was under contract to Collins and unhappy that he left in St. Paul to join Nat at the Tiffany Club, but came to hear them nightly.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And he was a little -- I don't know whether I said this before but when I ---he really didn't want me to join Nat because we had quite a good thing going. And I was under contract to him. I might have mentioned this before, but he finally said, okay, John, if you must go, because Nat was pretty good and making quite a bit of money at that time. And this was a step, financially for me, you know, a step forward financially for me. But musically where do you go from Art?

But any way, I wondered about it. I left him in St. Paul, Minnesota. I flew to California and joined Nat at the Tiffany Club, and I wondered how Art really felt about it. I knew he was a little peeved with me, and with Nat, but as soon as he came to California I looked up at night and there he was in the Tiffany to see. Because -- to see us. He loved Nat and he loved me. So every night he was there and when he became ill he stayed home quite a bit.
